# OpenAEC BIM Validator

> Open-source, browser-based IFC validation against IDS specifications,
> with a 3D viewer and BCF export. Built by 3BM Bouwkunde. Free to use;
> also available as a Windows desktop app and a command-line tool.

## What it does

- Validates IFC building models (IFC2X3 and IFC4) against buildingSMART
  IDS (Information Delivery Specification) files.
- Ships two Dutch standards out of the box: NL BIM Basis ILS v2 and
  RVB BIM Norm v1.1 (Rijksvastgoedbedrijf).
- Reports each specification as passed, failed or **not checkable** — a
  specification the engine cannot evaluate (e.g. its ifcVersion does not
  cover the model schema) is never silently passed or failed.
- 3D viewer with spatial tree, element properties, isolation (ghost
  mode), section planes and multi-model federation.
- Exports issues as BCF 2.1 for use in any BCF-compatible tool.
- Project containers with cloud storage (.wefc project envelopes),
  multi-tenant aware.

## Interfaces

- **Web app**: upload an IFC, pick a standard or custom IDS, validate,
  inspect failing elements in 3D, export BCF.
- **CLI**: `ifc-validate model.ifc --ids nl-bim` — console, HTML and
  JSON output; exit codes for CI pipelines. Batch-friendly.
- **MCP server**: `python -m ifc_validator.mcp_server` — Model Context
  Protocol over stdio for AI assistants. Tools: `validate_ifc`,
  `list_standards`, `export_report`. Validation runs locally via
  IfcOpenShell/ifctester; model data never leaves the machine and no
  API key is needed.
- **REST API**: `/api/v1/validate` (async validation jobs, BCF export),
  `/api/v2/projects` (project containers, models, spatial tree,
  element properties).
- **Desktop app**: Windows installer with an embedded validation
  server; file associations for .ifc/.ifcx; sign-in with OpenAEC.

## Typical workflows

1. Quick check: upload IFC → choose NL BIM Basis ILS → validate →
   review failing elements per specification in the 3D view.
2. CI gate: `ifc-validate model.ifc --ids rules.ids --format json`,
   fail the pipeline on non-zero exit.
3. Issue handoff: validate → select failing elements → export BCF →
   import in the modelling tool of choice.
4. AI-assisted review: connect the MCP server to an AI assistant and
   ask it to validate a model and explain which requirements fail and
   why.

## Technology

Python (FastAPI, IfcOpenShell, ifctester) backend; React/TypeScript
viewer on That Open Engine; open source.
